rows.grounds: locative plural of pañcāṅgulī, the five fingers
genitive dual of kara, the two hands
locative singular of brahmarandhra, the crown aperture
locative singular of mukha, the mouth
locative singular of hṛd, the heart

items.question: Which bodily loci receive the Śrīvidyā nyāsa after the crown placement?
premises: Śrīvidyā is placed on the crown in the previous verse.
The five fingers of the hands are named as a nyāsa locus.
Brahmarandhra, mouth, and heart are named as nyāsa loci.
items.inference: The nyāsa extends from the crown to the fingers, brahmarandhra, mouth, and heart.
uncertainties: The exact ritual order and function of each locus are not specified.
items.plain_english: On the five fingers of the hands, in the brahmarandhra, in the mouth, and in the heart.
